name: CO2 capture from ammonia plant, offsite
notes:
No CO2 Capture System, Only Compression

Reference: DOE/NETL-2022/3319
Hughes, Sydney, Zoelle, Alex, Woods, Mark, Henry, Samuel, Homsy, Sally, Pidaparti, Sandeep, Kuehn, Norma, Hoffman, Hannah, Forrest, Katie, Sheriff, Alana, Fout, Timothy, Summers, William, and Herron, Steve. Cost of Capturing CO2 from Industrial Sources. United States: N. p., 2022. <https://doi.org/10.2172/1887586>.

1. Purpose of Each Energy Input (from top to bottom)
    a) Electricity - CO2 capture system
    b) Natural Gas - Steam generation for CO2 capture system
    c) Electricity - CO2 compression after capture
    d) Electricity - CO2 pipeline transportation electricity for booster pump(s)

2. Default Electricity Source:
    a) Capture and Compression - Renewable (Wind) (on-site electricity source)
    b) Pipeline transportation - U.S Mix (off-site electricity source)

3. Zero capture energy (electricity and natural gas) for the high purity CO2 sources (Ethanol, Ammonia, and Natural Gas Processing)
    a) There is no CO2 capture system because CO2 purity is already high. 

4. Electricity for CO2 pipeline transportation
    a) This is to deliver CO2 by a 200-miles pipeline with one booster pump.
    b) The electricity demand for one booster pump is 7.653541 MJ/metric ton of CO2 with the following conditions: 
        - Pressures fixed: 2200 psia and 1500 psia 
        - Transportation temperature = 25 degC
        - Booster pump efficiency = 70%
        - # of booster: at every 100 miles
